correctness.rationale: For r=2p+3≥7, Massri’s hypothesis p>N=1 holds, giving the integral codimension-three scheme and its three-quadric ideal. In odd degree the invariant pairing is alternating and the binary-quadratic summand of Sym²(V) occurs once, so the transvectant and nonzero moment map have the same coordinate ideal. The differentiated pairing identifies rank failure with a nonzero infinitesimal stabilizer. A semisimple generator has no zero weight; a nilpotent generator has a pure-power kernel. Pure powers are zeros. Homogeneity at a nonzero zero makes the radial direction a kernel direction, so the affine rank test also gives the projective one. On a₀=1 the unipotent substitution x↦x+sy changes a₁ to a₁+s, giving an actual product of the a₁=0 slice with a smooth coordinate, not just a tangent-space complement. Directly differentiating in binomial coordinates gives q₀=2a_(r−1)+P₀ and q₁ linear in a_r with coefficient 2. The two terms of q₂ involving a_(r−1) add to −2(r−1)a₂a_(r−1), yielding the printed reduced equation. Its Hessian in a₃,…,a_(r−2) is invertible at t=0. Uniqueness of the stationary section makes it equivariant under the diagonal weights, hence the critical value is a single power c t^((r+1)/2). If c=0, the actual product chart would have slice singularities off the pure-power curve, contradicting the rank test. Completing squares, taking analytic units locally, and rescaling gives the asserted germ; the transverse Jacobian and Tjurina algebras are both C[t]/(t^((r−1)/2)). As a normalization check, at r=7 the reduced equation is 180t²a₄−120ta₃²+30a₃a₅−20a₄², with stationary value 405t⁴.
residual_risks: No assertion about the full nonreduced Jacobian scheme or global gluing of the local factors. The finite verification is supplementary, not evidence for arbitrary degree on its own.

originality.rationale: Credit the integral complete intersection to Massri, and the inclusion of the rational normal curve in the singular support to his earlier work. The supported distinct contribution is the exact rank-drop locus and the uniform transverse analytic A-type; the inspected tangent-cone and cotangent-shell theorems do not yield both assertions. There are two distinct indexed records with genuinely equivalent local classifications, one in a larger odd-degree range and the other with an added Jacobian-scheme assertion. Their publication entries are later than the frozen publication entry, while the common first-public-date metadata equals that of the underlying Massri preprint; this does not independently date the overlap or establish priority. Both comparisons are retained. No earlier statement or routine prior implication of the analytic classification was verified.
residual_risks: Earlier equivalent work in invariant theory or symplectic geometry could exist; the broad web query did not return useful coverage. The relationship between the exact archive overlaps is unresolved, and the comparison does not certify absolute priority.

value.rationale: The family is a natural equivariant complete intersection already singled out by its osculating hull. Identifying its only singular stratum and the uniform transverse ADE type, with an explicitly degree-dependent Milnor number, is substantial local geometry beyond the known tangent cone or singular inclusion. These are useful inputs to studying the family's vanishing cycles or resolutions; no such global theorem is claimed.
